findings.title: Ransomware.live victim entry: NVIDIA, group Thegentlemen
findings.summary_md: Ransomware.live indexed an entry for NVIDIA on The Gentlemen's extortion site at 09:22 UTC on November 18, 2026, with an estimated attack date of November 18 and the tracker status pending. The listing gives nvidia.com, the ticker NVDA and a revenue figure, and the field where sample data would normally appear says only DATA INFO - SOON; no stolen files are attached. The tracker records a negotiation Tox identifier and Hudson Rock infostealer counts of 353 compromised employees, 1,115,967 compromised users, 327 third-party employee credentials and 181 external attack surface findings, which describe background exposure rather than evidence of this intrusion.

findings.title: Nvidia faces ransom demands from The Gentlemen: leak timer under 10 days
findings.summary_md: Cybernews reported on November 18, 2026, that Nvidia faced ransom demands from The Gentlemen after the group added the chipmaker to its dark web leak site. The article said a countdown timer showed 234 hours, less than 10 days, until the alleged leak would activate. The reporting treated the entry as a claim rather than a confirmed breach, and cited researcher Aras Nazarovas urging caution because the group had previously named the wrong victims and reused data from earlier incidents.

findings.title: No Manners Here: The Ruthless Rise of The Gentlemen Ransomware
findings.summary_md: Unit 42 profiled The Gentlemen, also tracked as Storm-2697, as a ransomware-as-a-service program active since at least July 2025 that grew out of an affiliate relationship with Qilin. It counted 580 claimed victims across 77 countries through July 7, 2026, including 103 in manufacturing, with 117 claims in June 2026 alone. The report lists exploited bugs CVE-2024-55591, CVE-2025-32433, CVE-2025-33073 and CVE-2025-55182, plus CVE-2025-7771 in ThrottleStop.sys, and recommends alerts on scheduled tasks matching the string gentlemen*, EDR tamper protection, and monitoring for wevtutil, vssadmin and wmic abuse.
